properties.name: Apedemak the Lion God
properties.summary: Apedemak, the lion-headed warrior god of Kush, was worshipped as the supreme war deity. His temple at Naqa features him dispensing prisoners to the Meroitic king. The warrior queen Amanirenas invoked Apedemak when she led Kushite armies against Roman Egypt, famously losing an eye in battle but winning favorable terms.

properties.name: Jebel Barkal — Sacred Mountain of Creation
properties.summary: The Nubians believed Jebel Barkal was the primordial mound of creation where the god Amun dwelt inside the mountain. A natural rock pinnacle resembled a uraeus (royal cobra), confirming divine presence. This sacred geography legitimized Kushite kings as true pharaohs, heirs to the original creation.

properties.name: The Warrior Queens (Kandakes)
properties.summary: The Kandakes (warrior queens) of Kush were both political rulers and living goddesses. Amanirenas led armies against Augustus's Rome, blinding herself in battle. Amanishakheto accumulated enormous treasure. They ruled with divine authority from Apedemak, building pyramids and temples that rivaled Egypt's achievements.
